I've been playing since season one, across multiple platforms: PS4, Switch, and PC. It's been a fun few years. It has been my go-to after the deaths of the Titanfall and Halo franchises, and I've had a love/hate relationship with Apex for a long time. When this game started it was crazy. Every new addition was over-powered, every new thing was fun, and the "meta" was a concept far from my casual attitude towards the game. But as the game has progressed, it's left its casual players behind, and I get a sinking feeling that half of the people I face are using some sort of cheating software or mods to their keyboard to make impossible movement possible. Or, they're semi-pro. I love the drops, I love the weapons, I love the gameplay. I love the maps, and the scenery. I love the awesome abilities of the legends. But most every time I get into a firefight, the person in front does a three directional move in the air several times before my second shot has been fired. Or sometimes, I get shot in the skull three times from a Wingman cross map, when I can't even see the opponent through my scoped rifle. It's not an instant death for me: I know how the game works. I never give up, in game, and am long past the point of rage-quitting. But it isn't fun for me anymore. I'm not whining, because I don't want the game to change. I think I've just been addicted to it for a long time, and I think I'm past the place where I need to move on, as a casual player (and someone who knows everything about Apex, but doesn't reach out of gold ever). Wildcard was my jam for a while, but even that feels kinda like slamming into the opponent every two seconds and hoping that they break first. And that's cool! But...its just not fun for me anymore. My recommendation is to anyone thinking of trying Apex: It looks cool and flashy and feels great, but I don't think you'll have fun. Or you'll be like me and get an unhealthy addiction to it, and only get on to be frustrated. For those of you who still play, power to you. I hope you're having fun. I sure did. And if anyone happens to read this, please give me a recommendation for a new addictive game.

[update 2025-04-03] It's worse now. After 6 months I gave it another chance after reading dev posts about fixing matchmaking. As an average player, I can barely win a 1v1 against a diamond player, 1 out of 5 times. Now all my lobbies are full of master and even pred banners, both ranked AND mix. You think cheaters are bad? You think gamepad players with legal aimbot autoaim are bad? Hold my beer. Try playing against elites who mastered this game. It doesn't matter anymore if they play with you or against you, nothing you do matters, nothing. If you manage to win, it feels worse than having your team wiped on landing by one player. And sitting on top of it all is the dingleberry crowning this turd pie, the rank spread ribbon, dishonest, misleading and fake, it hides the lobby's actual skill spread behind the meaningless rank badges of the current season, which get reset all the time. Serves me right for believing their lies I guess.  skinner box matchmaking  After playing this game for so many hours, I noticed that matchmaking system behaves like a skinner box for players. To make the game as addictive as possible, you use random intermittent rewards in the form of good matches. A good match doesn't mean you win. Winning a match full of newbie teams feels as bad as being put into a shark tank full of multi-season preds, and so does being put together with a pro who carries you the entire match. A good match is when you get to play with people close to your skill level, give or take, when the match feels fair and that you had a chance. This is what a skill based matchmaking system would do. Apex Legends matchmaking doesn't do that. What it does, is no matter if you play unranked, ranked, ranked right after a reset, or ranked 2-3 weeks in, it places you into bad matches most of the time, with a few good matches sprinkled in strategically here and there. If you're playing semi-regularly, you can almost plot an exponential decay curve of good matches after every 1-2 week break you take, or after a new rank reset: in the beginning almost half of the matches is good, but the more you play, the worse the ratio becomes, until you can spend an entire evening and not even get one match that feels fair. Take a break for a week or two, the curve resets, you get more good matches again. After playing this game for many years, the pattern is as obvious and predictable as clockwork. How does it achieve this? There are two factors that have a huge impact on how good the match will be for a solo player: his teammates, and the other 19 teams that make up a battle royale match. The matchmaking system controls both. Players who party up still leave 19 teams to be chosen by the system, so even if you stack up a good party, the system can put you against a match of stacked preds, and there's nothing you can do, barring dumb luck.  I was going to mention rampant cheating, both hack-based stuff like aimbots and maphacks, and "legal" cheats like exploited aim assists and modded macro-gamepads, but who cares? If you aren't a very skilled player, like I am, what difference does it make if the system put you with top 0.1% honest pro player preds or with aimbot cheaters? Both wipe the floor with you, and both will just run forward and kill everything ahead when they're in your team.  Given these issues, the paid battle pass "controversy" feels  astroturfed. Apex Legends has what felt like the best multiplayer FPS mechanics in years, it's such a shame that its owners have a need to recoup the costs by designing such a hostile matchmaking system that exploit players. I would have preferred them making it an honest paid game, subscription or one time.
